hints.text: Check whether $3$ and $5$ share any factor other than $1$. When two numbers share none, their least common multiple has a simple form.
Both numbers are prime, so the only common factor is $1$. In that case the LCM is the product of the two numbers: work out $3 \times 5$.
$3 \times 5 = 15$, so the least common multiple is $15$.

explanation: $3$ and $5$ are both prime, so they share no common factor other than $1$.
When two numbers share no factors, the smallest number both divide is their product.
Multiply to find it: $3 \times 5 = 15$. The lists $3, 6, 9, 12, 15$ and $5, 10, 15$ confirm this.
So the least common multiple of $3$ and $5$ is $15$.
